title: Create a shipments table
prompt: Create a table named shipments with four columns, all of which must have a value. id is an integer and the primary key. order_id is an integer that must be the id of an existing order. weight_kg is numeric(6, 2) and must be greater than 0. shipped_on is a date.
hints: Which column depends on another table, and which has a limit on its value?
REFERENCES links order_id to orders (id). CHECK holds the test on the weight.
order_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES orders (id), weight_kg numeric(6, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (weight_kg > 0)
verify: INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (1, 5, 2.50, '2025-03-01') RETURNING id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on;
rejects: INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (2, 999, 1.00, '2025-03-01')
INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (3, 5, 0, '2025-03-01')
INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (4, NULL, 1.00, '2025-03-01')
INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (5, 5, 1.00, NULL)
INSERT INTO shipments (id, order_id, weight_kg, shipped_on) VALUES (1, 6, 1.00, '2025-03-02')

wrongAnswers.misconception: Leaves out the link to orders, so any order_id is accepted.

feedback: The feedback names an INSERT that should have been rejected. Find the rule that would stop that row.
